data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin name ‘Januarius’, meaning ‘youthful, generous, or tender’. In Christian tradition, Januarius is the patron saint of the sick and those suffering from fever. The name Genaro carries the meaning “Generous, Tender” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Genaro usually hope their child will grow to embody generous, tender and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, St. Januarius or Genaro is the patron saint of Naples, Italy. This mystic saint is known for his miraculous powers in healing the sick, particularly those suffering from fever. The relics of this saint, in the form of preserved leaking blood, are believed to possess miraculous properties, offering solace, hope, and strength to those in need. The tale of St. Januarius is deeply rooted in Italian spirituality, and invoking his name is believed to bring succor and relief to the afflicted.
